results.why: K26 scores exactly the explicit numbered/parenthesised enumeration formatting used to itemize contributions, which is T01's core property, while K09's connective counting mixes in non-enumerative transitions and is a different channel.

The numeric-density candidates (K04, K10, K20, K24, K33) all score all specific performance figures — BLEU, speedups, error rates, counts — and are clearly broader than a count restricted to percentage-formatted numbers.
No candidate scores the parenthetical-example habit ('(e.g., ...)', '(i.e., ...)'); the nearest connective channels (K31, K09) count sentence-opening transitions instead.
K50 counts named, recognizable benchmarks and datasets by proper name, the same counting operation as T04, whereas K48 is broader in centering external named models and systems generally.

K40 scores how technically accessible the opening is and K47/K32 score whole-abstract framing or template sequence, none of which isolates whether the first sentence is a generic field-importance platitude.

No candidate scores the advertising of experiment counts ('extensive experiments on six benchmarks'); the numeric-density channels count result figures and K50 counts benchmark names, not scale claims.

K14, K19, and K45 each score the density of unrendered LaTeX/markup residue (commands, math delimiters, escapes, footnote markers) exactly as T07 does, while K49 additionally folds in placeholders, hyphenation, and spacing and is broader.
No candidate scores efficiency register vocabulary (efficient, lightweight, scalable, low-cost); speedups appear only as numeric figures inside the benchmark-arithmetic channels.
No candidate scores a question-posed-and-answered rhetorical structure; the template channels (K32, K39) score the opposite, conformity to the problem-gap-method-results sequence.
K34 scores the extent of promotional adjectives, adverbs, and emphatic claims, which is the same hype-register count as T10.
K07 rates explicit priority/originality claims ('first', 'to our knowledge', 'unprecedented') with the same instruction not to judge their truth, matching T11 directly.
No candidate scores membership in the graph-learning/GNN subfield; K35 targets applied real-world domains and K06/K11/K37 target trendy AI vocabulary.
